description: Composite business-rule examples: multiple operators combined, matching the kind of requirement this skill is usually asked to encode.

examples.name: eligible for discount
examples.requirement: Customer gets a discount if they are a loyalty member AND have spent over $100, OR if it's their birthday month.
examples.explanation: First branch (loyalty member AND spent > $100) is truthy, so `or` short-circuits and returns true without needing the birthday check.

examples.name: required fields present before validating
examples.requirement: Only evaluate the age check if age was actually provided.
examples.explanation: `missing` returns a non-empty (truthy) array when 'age' is absent, so the outer `if` short-circuits to 'incomplete' instead of evaluating the age comparison.

examples.name: any item over a threshold
examples.requirement: Flag an order if any line item exceeds $500.
examples.explanation: Inside `some`'s test, `var` is relative to each array element, not the top-level data object.

examples.name: empty-array edge case
examples.requirement: Same rule as above, but demonstrating the empty-array behavior worth double-checking (see references/operations.md).
examples.explanation: `some` is false on an empty array — no items means nothing can exceed the threshold.
